title: arXiv mathematics — weekly notable papers (26 September–2 October 2026)
global_caveat: This is an inferred qualitative notable-paper selection, not an official arXiv trending chart. Citation and attention evidence is too sparse to establish popularity; order reflects claimed result specificity and cross-field reach, not measured readership.

sections.title: Singularity of harmonic measures for hyperbolic lattices
sections.abstract: For cocompact hyperbolic lattices containing a convex-cocompact codimension-one subgroup, the author proves singularity of hitting measures for every finitely supported admissible random walk, extending the singularity conjecture to several classes of lattices.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that each finitely supported admissible walk on the specified lattice has hitting measure singular to visual/Lebesgue measure and derives the singularity conjecture for listed classes including cocompact Kleinian groups.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Cocompact lattice in Isom(H^n), n ≥ 2, containing a convex-cocompact codimension-one subgroup in Sageev's sense; the walk is finitely supported and admissible.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem does not cover every cocompact hyperbolic lattice; it assumes the specified codimension-one subgroup.

sections.title: On Greenberg's conjecture for rational elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes
sections.abstract: For rational elliptic curves with ordinary reduction at an odd prime and a rational prime-degree isogeny, the authors prove Greenberg's conjecture on vanishing algebraic Iwasawa μ-invariants and confirm a related conjecture for analytic μ-invariants.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the stated Greenberg conjecture case and confirm Stevens's conjecture on analytic μ-invariants via the Iwasawa Main Conjecture for elliptic curves at Eisenstein primes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: E/Q has ordinary reduction at an odd prime p and admits a rational p-isogeny.
sections.unique_caveat: The claim is limited to the stated rational-isogeny/Eisenstein-prime setting, not all elliptic curves or ordinary primes.

sections.title: Minimal submanifolds and waists of locally symmetric spaces
sections.abstract: The authors establish higher-dimensional topological expansion for compact locally symmetric manifolds associated with SL(n,R) and more general split simple groups, using minimal-submanifold volume bounds, and give a locally symmetric example of power-law systolic freedom.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show higher d-expansion for the specified locally symmetric families for d ≤ n/8 in the SL(n,R) case and d linear in rank for split simple groups; they also report the first locally symmetric example of power-law systolic freedom.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact locally symmetric manifolds with universal cover the symmetric space of SL(n,R) or a split simple non-compact real Lie group, within the stated dimension/rank ranges.
sections.unique_caveat: The result applies to the specified families and dimension/rank ranges, not arbitrary locally symmetric spaces; the authors say the paper partially supersedes earlier work.

sections.title: Central Limit Theorems for Finitary Factors of iid Processes
sections.abstract: For multidimensional random fields that are finitary factors of iid processes, the authors derive central limit theorems with explicit rates and Brownian-sheet weak convergence under coding-radius tail decay conditions, with applications to statistical-mechanics models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish explicit CLT convergence rates and weak convergence to a Brownian sheet for suitably regular observables under conditions on coding-radius tail decay.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A multidimensional random field is a finitary factor of iid; the observable is suitably regular and the coding-radius tail satisfies the paper's decay conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not claim a CLT for all finitary factors; rates and convergence depend on tail and regularity hypotheses.

sections.title: Galois groups of random polynomials of large degree
sections.abstract: For random monic integer polynomials with independent bounded coefficients, the authors bound the probability of a square discriminant under a Rényi-entropy condition and combine it with prior results to obtain full symmetric Galois groups with high probability under additional hypotheses.
sections.claimed_result: Unconditionally, P(discriminant is a square) = O_mu(1/log n) when order-2 Rényi entropy H2(mu) > 12; with previous results and further assumptions this yields full Sym(n) Galois group with high probability when conditioned on omega_0 ≠ 0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Independent uniformly bounded integer-valued coefficients; omega_1 through omega_(n-1) share a law mu with H2(mu) > 12; the full-Galois-group conclusion additionally requires the paper's hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The entropy threshold is sufficient, and the full symmetric-group conclusion is not unconditional on that threshold alone.

sections.title: A centerpoint theorem for three planar convex bodies
sections.abstract: For three planar convex bodies satisfying a midpoint containment condition, the authors prove a sharp 2/9 halfspace centerpoint guarantee, settling the three-slice case of Oertel's mixed-integer centerpoint conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: For planar convex bodies A0,A1,A2 with 1/2(A0+A2) contained in A1, the authors prove a centerpoint with every containing closed halfspace capturing at least 2/9 of total area; they state this is best possible.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Exactly three planar-convex-body slices with the middle body containing the Minkowski midpoint of the outer two, in Z × R^2.
sections.unique_caveat: This treats the three-slice, two-dimensional case and does not alone resolve the conjecture for arbitrary dimensions or numbers of slices.
